instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are TEN questions in this paper.

subQuestions.text: Give the comparison among ionic, covalent and metallic bonds.
What effect would you expect in different types of bonds on strength, ductility and conductivity?
Define a space lattice. What are its important characteristics?

Describe briefly the following with neat sketches:
(i) BCC structure
(ii) FCC structure
(iii) HCP structure
(iv) Miller indices
Show from the fundamental principle, the atomic packing factor for FCC and BCC structures are $0.74$ and $0.68$ respectively. Also determine its coordination number.
Copper has an FCC structure and an atomic radius of $1.278\text{ \AA}$. Calculate its density. Atomic weight of copper is $63.5$ and Avogadro's number $= 6.023 \times 10^{23}$.

Define and explain briefly the following terms giving suitable sketches:
(i) Point defects
(ii) Line defects
(iii) Schottky defects
(iv) Edge and screw dislocations
(v) Burger's vector
What is the difference between impurities and alloying elements? Name a few impurities present in steel.
Distinguish clearly among the conductor, semiconductor and insulator of electricity using the energy band diagram model.
What is a semiconductor? Name the various semiconductor materials. What is the difference between n-type and p-type semiconductors?
Distinguish between soft magnetic material and hard magnetic material. Give a few examples of each type indicating their composition and applications.
Draw a typical $B-H$ curve for ferromagnetic material and explain the significance of nature of the curve.
Explain the basic mechanism involved in solid solution hardening and give examples of alloys strengthened by this process.
How does the plastic deformation in polycrystalline metals differ from that of single crystal?

questions.text: Draw the complete iron-carbon phase diagram and discuss briefly the structure and properties of steel having $0.83\%$ and $0.43\%$ carbon when cooled from $1000\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ to room temperature.

subQuestions.text: Why is martensite so hard and brittle?
Why is damping capacity of ductile iron better than steel?
Why is glass used mostly as reinforcement material for composites?
Why continuous cooling of plain carbon steel does not show bainite in its microstructure?

Give the composition, properties and uses of the following alloys:
(i) High-speed steel
(ii) Silicon steel
(iii) Stainless steel
(iv) Vanadium steel
(v) Tungsten steel
What are the commercial alloys of aluminium? Briefly describe their composition and uses.
